Wind Capacity Factor: CODERS vs renewables.ninja

Introduction

This report compares capacity factor data across two wind energy datasets. Each source dataset contains the hourly capacity factor for wind generation for each MERRA-2 map cell across the Canadian provinces. We examine the standard deviation across a region's map cells for each hour. We should expect to see variation in most hours, since wind speeds are rarely consistent across an entire province. Some hours should have quite high variation as larger wind systems move across the region. In this summary, we examine the standard deviation across both a single province (British Columbia), and across all Canadian provinces.

Descriptive Statistics

The following box plot compares the distribution of hourly standard deviations for each sample, for British Columbia.a and across all cells. We observe that the standard deviation is very low at almost all hours in the CODERS sample. The renewables.ninja sample shows much higher standard deviation, and a larger range of deviations across hours of the year.

Graphs

Capacity factor standard deviation in British Columbia.a

The following chart shows the standard deviation of the capacity factor across cells in a single balancing area, per hour of the year. British Columbia is chosen here because it is a large geographical area where we should expect variation in wind patterns across the province in any given hour, from the windy coast to the interior where there is much less wind.

Capacity factor standard deviation across Canada

As a reference, this chart shows the standard deviation of the capacity factor across all of Canada for each hour of the year. We should see high variation in most hours for wind capacity factor. Again we observe a much lower standard deviation in the CODERS dataset.

Conclusion

In this report we examined the standard deviation in wind power across cells in the same hour, for each hour of the year. We compared results across two wind power datasets, one from CODERS, and the other from renewables.ninja. We observed that the CODERS dataset exhibited exremely low standard deviation, suggesting that wind power was consistant across an entire province in any given hour. This is an unexpected result, and suggests that the CODERS data was generated using some constant factor in each province that is resulting in over-normalized data across each balancing area.
